clue.text: A bit of dissipation in the courtyard

indicators.note: only a bit of the word dissipation is wanted, a run of letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A little debauchery going on out in the courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved open yard beside or within a house, a kind of courtyard.

clue.text: Not many people in this public institution

definitions.text: Not many people in this public institution

parts.words: Not many people in this public institution
parts.note: read literally it is the old parish home for paupers

explanation.surface: A public body that draws hardly any visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a description of a sparsely attended venue, but the phrase also names the workhouse once run for the destitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, a parish-run home housing paupers was a public institution for the destitute.

clue.text: Bear going over a mile to get to the Pole?

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece goes over, above, the second

parts.note: to tote is to carry, to bear
M is the abbreviation for mile

explanation.surface: A bear trekking more than a mile to reach the North Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by association: the answer is the word that goes before 'pole' in the carved tribal post, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved emblem post is called a totem pole, so the word partners 'pole'.

clue.text: Put off moronic old character

indicators.note: put off suggests the word moronic knocked out of shape, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told to deter a stupid elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is a letter of the ancient Greek alphabet, an old written character.

clue.text: Reform involving double degree in one's university

indicators.note: involving means one piece wraps around, takes in, the other

parts.note: to reform something is to alter it

indicators.note: double asks for the degree abbreviation written twice in succession

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A college changes its rules so students can take two degrees at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater, Latin for nourishing mother, is the term for the university or school someone attended.

clue.text: As investigators stated, they are Mexican Indians

indicators.note: stated means the phrase is spoken out loud and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: AS plus 'TECS, slang short for detectives, the investigators

explanation.surface: Police detectives reporting on an indigenous people of Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they are' is a link. 'Tec is old slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztec people ruled central Mexico before the Spanish conquest, an Indigenous American nation.

clue.text: Plastered, hit by droppings from on high

definitions.meaning: covered with builder's cement, as bricks and a wall are

definitions.text: hit by droppings from on high
definitions.meaning: bombarded by shells lobbed high by a short-barrelled gun

explanation.surface: Drunk, and struck by something falling from the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' looks like drunk; it means rendered with cement. The second sense is being shelled by high-arcing artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bricklayers bind and coat with a lime-cement paste; a short cannon lobbing shells shares the name.

clue.text: One directing "The Silver King' is after leading male

indicators.note: is after says the silver and king pieces come after the leading male piece

parts.note: a man is a male
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
ER, Edward Rex, is the abbreviation for a king

explanation.surface: Someone staging a play called The Silver King is hunting for a male lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs or directs a business or team is its boss, the person in charge.

clue.text: Sticky wicket — fast spinner's taken over

parts.note: fast, as in held fast, means tight

indicators.note: taken over means the word is turned over, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy, so spinner's gives TOPS

explanation.surface: A cricket report: on a tricky pitch, the quick spin bowler has completed an over.
explanation.walkthrough: Sticky wicket is cricket for an awkward situation. 'fast spinner' suggests bowlers; the spinner is a toy top.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky wicket, from cricket, is a difficult situation, an awkward predicament.

clue.text: A revolver, whichever way it points

indicators.note: whichever way it points says the word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A handgun that is dangerous whichever way it is aimed.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning part of a helicopter or engine revolves, so it is something that revolves.

clue.text: He provides clothing that's striking and more appropriate

parts.note: workers on strike are out
fitter means more suitable

explanation.surface: A tailor whose wares are eye-catching and more suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shop or trader selling clothes and equipment.

clue.text: Dark horse ousting leader

indicators.note: ousting leader says the first letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: in chess the knight is the piece shaped like a horse

explanation.surface: An unknown racehorse has unseated the favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark horse' reads as one phrase; split it, Dark is the definition and horse the chess knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark, as in 'after dark', is the time between sunset and dawn.

clue.text: Though real crime is deplorable, it can produce great mirth

indicators.note: deplorable says the phrase is in a sorry state, its letters wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A remark that even dreadful crime can be very funny.
explanation.definitionFit: The epics of the ancient Greek poet describe the gods' unquenchable laughing, so the phrase means huge hilarity.

clue.text: Civilized old city destroyed by plague

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
a bane is a plague, a curse

explanation.surface: A refined ancient city wiped out by disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane means suave and polished in manner, courteous and refined.

clue.text: Spurned child put to bed?

parts.note: a boy is a child
jocular coinage: put in a cot, a child's bed

explanation.surface: A rejected youngster sent off to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shunned or rejected, as a product or event people refuse to support.

clue.text: Water tortoise secure on land

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the second piece after the first

parts.note: terra is Latin for land
to pin is to secure

explanation.surface: Tying up a turtle once it is ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, a tortoise of ponds and rivers.

clue.text: Tiny fish dominated by shark

indicators.note: dominated by in a down entry puts the fish under the shark

parts.note: the nurse is a species of shark
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A small fish lorded over by a shark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiny' looks like an adjective for the fish; it is a noun, a tiny, a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurseling is a baby being nursed, an infant, as a little one is a tiny.

clue.text: End up nursing girl, producing antacid

indicators.note: nursing means holding something within, as one piece cradles the other
up in a down entry means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an aim is an end, a goal
Agnes is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A nurse winds up caring for a girl and giving her stomach medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesia, magnesium oxide or hydroxide, is taken to neutralise stomach acid.

clue.text: Tiny page disguised as Arab

indicators.note: disguised says the letters of the phrase are dressed up in another order

explanation.surface: A little court servant in Arab costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt's people speak Arabic and count among the Arab nations.

clue.text: Get stall set up outside for flowers

indicators.note: outside says one piece stands round the other
set up in a down entry means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a stall in a theatre is a seat

explanation.surface: Someone told to erect a market stall outdoors for selling flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stall' suggests a market stand; it is a theatre seat, which turned upwards gives TAES around GET.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagetes is the botanical genus of marigolds, garden flowers.

clue.text: Feast the king found less colour

parts.note: Whit, Whitsun, is a church feast
ER, Rex, is the abbreviation for a king

explanation.surface: At a banquet the monarch turned pale.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitsun is the Christian festival of Pentecost.
explanation.definitionFit: Being paler means having less tint, closer to snow.

clue.text: It protects the head of conservative party

definitions.meaning: party here is a person: a reactionary, from US slang for construction workers seen as right-wing

explanation.surface: Headgear for the Tory leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' reads as a political party; it means an individual, as in 'the party concerned'.
explanation.definitionFit: A construction worker's helmet, and by extension a blue-collar reactionary.

clue.text: Harsh cries given by mother birds

parts.note: ma is mother
caws are the harsh cries of crows

explanation.surface: Mother birds squawking.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaws are large brightly coloured parrots, tropical birds.

clue.text: A girl usually expects to have such a hurried ceremony

definitions.text: A girl usually expects to have such a hurried ceremony

parts.words: A girl usually expects to have such a hurried ceremony
parts.note: 'expects' here means expecting a baby, so the rushed wedding is forced by a pregnancy

explanation.surface: A bride anticipating a quick wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is in 'expects': not looking forward, but pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding arranged in haste because the bride is pregnant, supposedly at a father's gunpoint.

clue.text: Vessel in deep waters capsizing

indicators.note: capsizing in a down entry turns the word upside down, read backwards

parts.note: pools are deep stretches of water

explanation.surface: A ship overturning in deep water.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a single-masted sailing boat.

clue.text: A new lot of paintings put up in empty chambers

indicators.note: put up in a down entry means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: art is a body of paintings

explanation.surface: Hanging a fresh collection of pictures in vacant rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Antra are anatomical cavities, hollow spaces in bone such as the sinuses.

clue.text: Musical group's love note produced in court

definitions.note: group's is group is, the 's a link

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: produced in puts the note within the court abbreviation

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A band's romantic song performed in a royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight musicians playing together form a band of that size.

clue.text: Order this tape containing German or Italian course

indicators.note: containing means the shuffled letters hold another piece within
order means put the letters of the phrase in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A diner asked to order a German or Italian dish from a tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin pasta is served as a dish, a course, in Italian meals.

clue.text: Do people we look up to have their support?

definitions.text: Do people we look up to have their support?

parts.words: Do people we look up to have their support?
parts.note: people we admire are placed on raised plinths, which literally hold them up

explanation.surface: A question whether our heroes enjoy backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' reads as backing; it is the stands under statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Columns or bases that hold up statues, figuratively raising admired people.

clue.text: Insect repelled round women's making a nasal sound

indicators.note: round means one piece goes about another
repelled means driven back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small insect
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A bug driven off by women who make a noise through their noses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns GNAT to TANG; 'round' puts it about W.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal quality of voice, a resonant tone.
